 Appearance:
 Shri Tapan Kumar Bathre - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Deepak Sahu - Panel Lawyer for the respondent-State.
 Order

This is the third application on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail in connection of with Crime No.53/2022 registered at Police Station Baihar, District Balaghat for the offence under Sections 302, 201, 376 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The applicant is in jail since 21.02.2022.

First and second applications of the applicant were dismissed as withdrawn vide orders dated 16th August, 2024 (Annexure A/2) and 13th February, 2023 (Annexure A/3) passed in M.Cr.C No.
37745/2022 and M.Cr.C. No.4395/2023 respectively.
On the last date of hearing, status report of the Sessions Trial has been called for.
That report was received by memo dated 08.07.2024.

The reason assigned in the said status report by the concerning Court does not tally with the reason for adjourning the case reflecting from ordersheets of the case filed by counsel for the applicant.
The delay in the trial is occurring due to non- availability of prosecution witnesses.

Although, the concerning Judge has 2 MCRC-21892-2024 assigned the reason that delay has occurred because counsel for the applicant is taking time when witnesses are present and refuse to examine them.
It is also showing in the memo that there was no instruction from the High Court for concluding the trial.
Surprisingly, the concerning Court before assigning reason as not verified the reason for delay.
It is also very surprising that concerning Court has written in the said memo that there was no instruction from the High Court for expediting the trial or concluding the same.
However, it is the duty of the Court to conclude the trial expeditiously and no adjournment be granted to the parties unnecessarily.
It is needless to say that concluding the trial expeditiously is the requirement of law and it is obligatory for the concerning Court.

sentences.text: 1 instruction from the High Court is required for the same.
The reason assigned by the concerning Judge is nothing but showing a casual attitude of the Court and the manner in which trial is dealt with.

In the previous application (M.Cr.C. No.4395 of 2023), this Court on 13.02.2023 has already directed the Court below to conclude the trial expeditiously but it appears that the concerning Court has not seen that ordersheet also which is apparent from the memo because incorrect information has been furnished.
Such a casual approach of the concerned Judge is highly deprecated.
Looking to the ordersheets filed by the learned counsel for the applicant and the fact that there is no adequate progress in the trial and Court is also not making any endeavour to get it done.

The period of custody of applicant is w.e.f. 21.02.2022 and looking to the delay in trial and the manner in which the trial has been dealt with, I am inclined to consider the application, though it is opposed by learned counsel for the State.
Accordingly, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with 3 MCRC-21892-2024 one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.

I t is further directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3)
of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to Principal District & Sessions Judge, Balaghat.
C.c. as per rules.
